facts.fact: Appleby, a law firm, describes the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act 2026 as enacted Mauritian law that recognises electronic signatures, electronic transferable records and contracts formed by automated message systems, amending the existing Electronic Transactions framework; no commencement date is given, and the as_of date is the article's published date.

Act No. 5 of 2026, the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act, was passed by the National Assembly on 19 May 2026 and assented to by the President on 25 May 2026; it comes into operation on a date to be fixed by Proclamation, different sections possibly on different dates, and the document gives no commencement date.

The Act amends an existing principal Electronic Transactions Act, repealing and replacing its section 8 on electronic signatures and section 18 on secure electronic records, and inserting new Part IIA and sections 14A to 14D and 15A on transferable records, automated contracts, online offers and foreign certificates; the document's date is that of assent.

note: The document concerns the Finance Act 2025 amendment of the Bills of Exchange Act for electronic transferable records, a narrow negotiable-instruments law of class other; it names no electronic transactions or e-commerce law.
